details.method:
In a heavy-bottomed stock pot, heat the oil over medium heat.
Lower the heat, add the salt, carrot, and onion and warm very gently, with the lid on, for about 5 minutes, or until the onion is softened and slightly
translucent but not brown.
Add the fish, thyme, garlic, and parsley then cover with a piece of paper, and re-cover the pot, letting the bones warm gently until they are slightly
opaque.
Remove the lid and the parchment; add the apple cider and turn up the heat until the stock starts to simmer.
Add the water, heat to a simmer, and let cook for 30 to 45 minutes.
Strain (you can remove fish first if that makes it easier), cool, and set aside for later use.

details.notes:
Sprinkle flour on the dough and place it on a lightly dusted rolling board. Avoid adding too much of the flour when rolling. Use sparingly and as needed.
Roll the dough out into a round or oval shape with a rolling pin.
You could pull the top part of the rolled dough with your fingers to make a tapering dough. 
Turn the rolled dough gently. Spread water all over the top side.
Next, heat a tawa or a flat skillet. Keep the heat to medium-high or high.
Place the watered side touching the hot skillet or tawa.
Cook for 1 to 2 minutes or until you see the base nicely browned and charred.
Using a spatula, separate the naan from the skillet. 
Lift the naan with tongs and place it on a direct flame with the side that is not cooked touching the flame.
Move the naan all over the flame to ensure the sides and the surfaces are well cooked with some chars.

details.notes: For the Curry SauceHeat a medium-sized pot over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the coconut oil. Once the coconut oil has melted, add the shallots to the pot and sauté for 1 minute.Next, add the garlic and ginger to the pot and cook for 30 seconds. Then add the curry leaves and black mustard seeds cook for 1-2 minutes to release all their flavor. Stir often to avoid burning.Next, add the curry powder, coriander, black pepper and salt to the pot and mix to combine with the other ingredients. Reduce the heat to medium and cook the spices, stirring often, for 3-4 minutes to allow them to cook through and become fragrant. If the pan is becoming too dry, add a splash of water to help the spices cook.Once the spices are cooked, add the tomato to the pot along with the tamarind paste (if using), soy sauce, fish sauce, sugar, the Thai Birds Eye chili pepper and cook for 2 minutes, stirring often.Add the water to the pot and bring the contents of the pot to a simmer over medium heat. Cover the pot with a lid and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. After 15 minutes, remove the lid of the pot and add the coconut milk. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for 5 minutes to allow the flavours to combine.

details.notes: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar and salt. With a pastry cutter or your fingers, gradually work the butter into the flour until pea-sized pieces form. In a small bowl, stir together the egg yolk and water, then stir into the flour mixture using a fork. Stir, then knead the dough together until it is no longer crumbly and holds together when pinched with your fingers. Form it into a disc and wrap it tightly with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a circle. Transfer the crust to a round fluted tart pan with a removable bottom. Press the crust into the pan and trim the edges. Place the crust in the refrigerator for 60 minutes (or freezer for 30 minutes). Preheat the oven to 210_x0002_ÚC during the last 20 minutes of chilling the crust. Line the inside of the crust with parchment paper, then fill with baking weights or dried beans. Bake until the edges of the crust are very lightly golden, 10 to 12 minutes. Remove the pie weights and parchment paper, and prick the bottom of the crust with a fork, 6 to 8 times. Return to the oven and bake until the whole crust is golden brown all over, 8 to 12 minutes longer. Let cool to room temperature

details.method:
Wash the chili peppers and remove the stems. If you prefer a milder sauce, you can remove some or all of the seeds. Chop the onion and mince the
garlic. In a saucepan, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Add the minced
garlic, 2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick, and 2 whole cloves to the pan. Sauté for another minute until fragrant. Pour in the white wine vinegar and
water. Add the sugar and salt, stirring to combine. Add the chili peppers to the saucepan and bring the mixture to a simmer. Allow the mixture to
simmer for about 10-15 minutes, until the peppers soften and the flavors meld together. Remove from heat and let it cool. Discard the bay leaves
and blend. You can use the sauce immediately or transfer it to a jar and refrigerate it for later use.

details.method:
Step 1:
Combine the milk powder and the water together.
Heat the milk until it is warm but not hot, about 90 degrees. In a large bowl, combine it with the yeast. Stir lightly, and let sit until the
mixture is foamy, about 5 minutes.
Step 2:
Using a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook, beat the eggs, butter, sugar and salt into the yeast mixture. Add half of the flour and mix
until combined, then mix in the rest of the flour until the dough pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Add more flour, if the dough is too wet, the dough will probably become too thick to beat; when it does, transfer it to a floured surface,
and gently knead it until smooth.
Grease a large bowl with a little oil. Transfer the dough to the bowl, and cover. Let rise at room temperature until it doubles in size,
about 1 hour.
Step 3:
Turn the dough out onto a well-floured surface, and roll it to ½-inch thickness. Cut out the doughnuts with a doughnut cutter, flouring
the cutters as you go. Reserve the doughnut holes. Knead any scraps together, being careful not to overwork,
and let rest for a few minutes before repeating the process.
Step 4:
Put the doughnuts on two floured baking sheets so that there is plenty of room between each one. Cover with a kitchen towel, and let
rise in a warm place until they are slightly puffed up and delicate, about 45 minutes.
Step 5:
About 15 minutes before the doughnuts are done rising, put the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat, and heat
it to 190°C.
Meanwhile, line cooling racks, baking sheets or plates with paper towels.
Step 6:
Carefully add the doughnuts to the oil, a few at a time, When the bottoms are deep golden, after 45 seconds to a minute, use a slotted
spoon to flip; cook until they’re deep golden all over.
Doughnut holes cook faster. Transfer the doughnuts to the prepared plates or racks, and repeat with the rest of the dough, adjusting the
heat as needed to keep the oil at 190°C.

details.notes: Mix the flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl and whisk to combine. Add the chopped chives, and parsley and mix one more to blend. Add in the Greek  yogurt. Then mix the olive oil with the fine chopped garlic, and pour that in, along with the water, Using a rubber spatula, combine the ingredients until a soft, moist dough forms, and all ingredients are well incorporated. No need to knead the dough. Turn the flatbread dough out onto a lightly floured work surface, and divide it into 6 equal portions, 100 to 120 grams each. Roll each portion into a ball shape. Take one flatbread dough ball and begin to gently press it out into a roughly 6 to 7 inch flatbread. The more rustic the better. Place onto a parchment-lined baking sheet to hold, while you repeat the process with the rest of the flat bread. Once all flatbreads are made, Heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Once hot, brush one side of one flatbread with olive oil, and place it into the skillet to cook for about 80 seconds, or until a deep golden-brown. Brush more olive oil over top and then flip and cook on this other side for about 80 seconds or until deep golden-brown. Once all flatbreads are cooked, brush a bit more olive oil over each, and sprinkle over a touch more parsley for garnish

details.ingredients: Bakery Flour (37.7%) (Wheat), Water (25.1%), Unsalted Natural Butter (25.1%) [Cow's Milk Fat, Bacterial Culture  ], Eggs (6%), White Sugar (2.5%), Instant Yeast (1.5%) [Yeast (Saccharomyces Cerevisae), Emulsifier: Sorbitan Monostearate E491 (From Vegetable Origin Raw Material: Palm Oil)], Alegria Semi Skimmed Milk Powder Nestle (1.5%) [Semi Skimmed Cow's Milk Powder, Emulsifier (Soya Lechithin)], Salt (0.38%) [Iodized Table Salt], Bread Improver (0.05%) [Flour (Wheat), Antioxidant E300, Enzyme (Alpha Amylase, Hemicellulases)]

details.method:
Preheat oven to 180*C.
Pour oil into a baking dish. Use a pastry brush to coat the bottom of the pan.
Transfer the risen dough to the prepared baking dish. Work the dough to the edges. Use your fingers to create dimples in the dough.
Using a pizza cutter or a sharp knife, make 3 equally-spaced slices across the short side of the baking dish*. Then, slice down the center of the
dough lengthwise to create a breadsticks.
Brush the top of the breadsticks with one teaspoon of olive oil.
Sprinkle the garlic powder and salt evenly over the breadsticks.
Bake for 18-20 minutes, or until golden brown.
Immediately brush the baked breadsticks with the remaining olive oil and sprinkle with parmesan cheese. Serve warm.

Preheat oven to 160*C.
With a rolling pin, roll dough into approximately an 18-inch-by-12-inch rectangle, 
just eyeball it.
Add the strawberry compote and spread evenly, leaving a small margin near edges.
Starting with a long side, roll to form a tight cylinder.
Slice the cylinder into 8 to 10 evenly sized pieces.
Compote will escape out; it s to be expected. Push back in what you can but don t worry about it.
Arrange the rolls in the prepared baking pan. Cover with plastic wrap.
Allow the rolls to rise in a warm, draft-free place until nearly doubled, about 60 to 75 minutes and then bake.

Combine whole milk, cream, and the split and  vanilla  and pod in a saucepot over medium-low heat and gently stir.
Bring to a simmer. Place the yolks in a mixing bowl, beat them. 
Add granulated sugar  and whisk until the mixture is combined.
To begin the tempering process, gradually ladle the hot milk and cream mixture into the mixing bowl one ladle at a time while whisking continuously.
The aim is to gradually heat the egg yolks to the temperature of the warm milk and cream so as not to curdle the eggs.
When the temperature of the yolks is similar to the temperature of the milk and cream, whisk the contents of the mixing bowl into the
saucepot with the remaining vanilla cream.
Swap your whisk for a flat-bottom spoon and continue to stir as you cook to 85 C. 
The cr me anglaise will be thickened and should coat the back of a spoon.
Test by swiping your finger across the back of the coated spoon. If the sauce is thickened, the swipe should remain and not be filled in
by runny sauce. Strain the cr me anglaise through a chinois into a mixing bowl resting in an ice bath. Remove the vanilla pod and set aside for future use.
Whisk to help cool to room temperature.

preheat oven to160*C . Line a muffin pan with baking cups/cupcake liners and set aside.
To a medium mixing bowl, add aerated flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and sea salt. Whisk to combine, and set aside.
To a small mixing bowl, add yogurt, lemon zest, and lemon juice, and stir to combine.
To a large mixing bowl, add eggs,  oil, and lemon yogurt mixture, and whisk to combine until pale and smooth. Add flour mixture, and gently fold with a spatula until almost combined (some of the flour should still be visible). Add raspberries, and gently fold until just incorporated.
Using a large cookie scoop, scoop batter into prepared muffin tin, distributing batter evenly among all the baking cups. Tap the muffin tin on the counter 2-3 times to settle the batter in the cups.
Spoon about 1 heaping tablespoon of streusel topping per muffin (evenly distributing topping). Bake for 20-25 minutes (see Note #5) until cooked through and light golden around the edges. Test for doneness by inserting a toothpick that comes out clean. Place the hot muffin pan on a wire cooling rack, and allow the muffins to rest in the pan for 5-10 minutes. Remove muffins and transfer to a wire cooling rack to cool. Serve slightly warm or at room temperature, and enjoy the moist and tender crumb of these muffins!

details.notes:
Preheat the oven to 160*C.
In a bowl, add the salt, baking powder and cinnamon.  Stir to combine and set aside.
Place eggs, buttermilk, oil, vanilla and whisk until combined. 
Gradually add brown and white sugar; whisk until the sugar is incorporated and dissolved. The mixture should be a rich brown color.
Add flour and pour in the wet ingredients, folding the dry ingredients into the wet.

Add date paste and pecans into batter and stir until all the ingredients are mixed through.  Bake in the oven for 5 minutes.

Preheat oven to 160*C.
In addition to about puff pastry,  pears, raisin, cinnamon, butter and brown sugar.
Chop the butter into small cubes and mix with the sugar, squashing the butter in with a  fork.
Peel and core the pear and chop into small pieces.  Then mix with the sultanas and ground cinnamon.
Roll out the pastry to form a rectangle about 25cm x 30cm and spread with the sugar-butter mix.
Sprinkle the spiced pear mix on top.
Starting at a long edge, roll as tightly as possible into a long log-shape, pushing in any mixture which falls out.  Cut off the ends if they have no filling in them.  Then, using a sharp knife, cut widthway into slices.

details.ingredients:

Pastry Cream - 500g
Golden Raisins - Tatco - 300g
White Sugar - Tamimi Markets - 200g
Water - 200ml
Egg Wash - 200g
details.notes:
Preheat the oven to 160*C
Transfer the chilled pastry cream to a bowl and loosen it up with a whisk.
Spread an even layer of pastry cream onto the chilled sheet of dough, leaving 1cm on one of the short sides.
Drain the raisins and sprinkle them over the pastry cream.
Wet the bare end of the dough with a bit of water, this will help seal the dough.
Start rolling up the dough from the opposite end of the side that you wet with water. Press down slightly when you get to the other end to help seal the log.
Wrap in plastic wrap and put in the fridge to set for about 10 minutes. This will help when you cut the slices later.
Prepare your baking sheets with sheets of parchment paper.
Remove the dough from the freezer and using a sharp knife, cut into  slices, approximately 1cm thick. Place each slice on the baking sheets, leaving ample enough room between each roll. They will almost double in size after baking.
If the end of the roll comes undone, simple tuck it under the main part of the roll. Use a cake spatula, flatten out the top of each roll and nudge them back into circle form if necessary. Brush each roll with egg wash, tops and the sides.
Put in a warm area and let proof for about 2 hours. Baking Once the rolls have proofed,
Brush each of the rolls with egg wash once again. 
Bake for about 15 minutes,  Transfer directly to a cooling rack.

details.notes:
In the bowl of a stand mixer, whisk together the flours, sugar, salt, and instant yeast.
Add the milk, water, and olive oil, and mix with the dough hook until you have a smooth dough, about 7 to 10 minutes. This is a sticky dough, so if you decide to knead by hand, I recommend stretching and folding it in a large bowl for several minutes.
Place the dough into an oiled bowl, cover with a towel or plastic wrap, and let rise until doubled, about 45 minutes to an hour. At this point, you can deflate the dough and let it rise a second time, or proceed to shape the dough.
Line two half sheet pans with parchment paper, preheat your oven to 220*C , and place a steam pan on the lowest rack of the oven 
Scrape the risen dough out onto a lightly floured work surface. Using a bench scraper, divide the dough into four equal pieces.
Form one piece of dough into a ball by folding the dough over itself. With floured hands, gently pat the dough into a rectangle, Fold the top and bottom of the longer sides toward the middle, and then pinch the dough together to form a log. Roll the dough over so that the seam side is on the bottom.
With floured hands, roll the ends of the dough back and forth until they are skinnier than the middle. Pick up the log and place it on the parchment lined baking sheet, and curve the ends around and pinch them together to form a "purse." Pat the thicker part of the dough to flatten it to about 3/4 inch thick. Cover loosely with oiled plastic wrap. Repeat with the other 3 pieces of dough. There should be two "purses" per half sheet pan.
Let the loaves rise until puffy, about 30 to 45 minutes.
When ready to bake, brush the loaves with the egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Add one cup of boiling water to the steam pan just before baking the bread.
Bake the loaves, one pan at a time, for 15 to 18 minutes, until the bread is golden,

Lightly oil a large bowl and transfer the dough to the bowl, rolling it to coat it with oil. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap.
Ferment at room temperature for 60 to 90 minutes, or until the dough doubles in size.
 Wipe the counter with a damp cloth and transfer the dough to the counter.
Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces. Shape the pieces into boules (or round rolls).

Bake for 5 to 8 minutes on the middle shelf in the oven to ensure that the center is baked. Transfer the baked muffins to a cooling rack and cool for at least 30 minutes.

details.method:
Assemble the Strudel:
1. Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F).
2. Place a large, clean kitchen towel on your work surface and lightly flour it.
3. Roll out the dough on the floured towel as much as you can. Then, gently stretch the dough using the back of your hands until it's very
thin (almost transparent) and measures about 60x80 cm. The dough should be thin enough to see through.
4. Brush the stretched dough with melted butter.
5. Sprinkle the toasted breadcrumbs evenly over the dough.
6. Spread the apple filling over the breadcrumbs, leaving a 2.5 cm border all around.
7. If using, sprinkle chopped nuts over the filling.
Roll and Bake:
1. Using the kitchen towel to help, carefully roll the dough starting from the longer side where the filling is closer to the edge. Tuck in the
sides as you roll to enclose the filling.
2. Place the strudel seam-side down on a parchment-lined baking sheet.
3. Brush the top of the strudel with melted butter.
4. Bake in the preheated oven for 40-45 minutes, or until the strudel is golden brown and crispy.
5. Remove from the oven and let it cool slightly.
Serve:
1. Dust the top of the strudel with powdered sugar.

details.method:
Prepare the Chicken: Wash the Chicken whole pieces and drain excess water. You can optionally marinate the mutton in some yogurt, salt,
and spices (coriander powder, cumin powder, and turmeric) for 30 minutes to an hour for better flavor.
Fry Onions and Temper Spices: In a large pan, heat ghee or oil over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Then, add the
sliced onions and sauté until golden brown and caramelized (around 10 minutes).
Add Ginger-Garlic Paste and Chilies: Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Cook until the raw smell disappears (about 2 minutes).
Cook the Chicken: Add the Chicken pieces to the pan and sear them until browned on all sides (about 5-7 minutes). This will give the
mutton a nice caramelization and flavor.
Add Spices: Sprinkle in the coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and garam masala powder. Stir well and let
the spices cook for a minute or two to release their aroma.
Incorporate Cashew or Almond Paste: Add the cashew paste or almond paste. Stir it in well to form a creamy base. If you're using poppy
seeds, you can grind them with a little water to make a paste and add it now.
Add Yogurt: Lower the heat and add the whisked yogurt, stirring continuously to avoid curdling. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until the
yogurt blends with the spices and forms a thick gravy.
Add Water: Pour in water to adjust the gravy to your desired consistency. You can make it more or less thick, depending on your
preference. Cover and cook the mutton for 40-45 minutes on low heat until the mutton becomes tender. If using a pressure cooker, cook for
about 15-20 minutes after the first whistle.
Add Cream and Lemon Juice: Once the mutton is cooked, add cream for a rich finish. Stir it in well, and then check for seasoning. Add salt
and a squeeze of lemon juice for a slight tanginess.
Garnish and Serve: Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.

In a bowl, combine the onion, celery, bell peppers, and garlic.
Remove 1½ cups of this mixture and transfer to a separate bowl (you'll add this to the gumbo toward the end).
Set both bowls aside.
In a large bowl, mix together the vegetable broth, canned tomatoes, fresh tomatoes, wine, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, 2
tablespoons of the parsley, the oregano, thyme, chili, and mustard.
Set aside.
In a large pot, heat the oil over medium-high heat.
Once it's hot, add the flour and stir constantly with a large wooden spatula, until it is well combined.
Reduce the heat to medium and continue stirring until the roux is dark brown,
15 to 20 minutes.
You need to toast the flour and oil while preventing the mixture from burning.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the larger amount of the onion mixture (not the reserved 1½ cups).
Continue cooking, stirring constantly, until the vegetables are soft, 4 to 6 minutes.
Mix in the Cajun spice to the vegetables and mix well.
Cook for another 5 minutes, stirring frequently, toasting the Cajun spice.
Add the broth mixture and bay leaves.
Mix well and bring to a boil, stirring often to prevent the bottom from burning. Once at a boil, cook for about 10 minutes.
add the vegan ball
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, to reduce and thicken the gumbo.
Add some of the spring onions, okra, the remaining parsley, and the reserved 1½ cups of the onion mixture.
If needed, add 1 to 2 cups water to loosen the gumbo.
Simmer for another 20 minutes.

Boil sugar and water until it reaches 120 degrees Celsius.
While waiting for the sugar to reach its temperature, beat remaining egg whites in the mixer until it becomes foamy.
Pour sugar syrup onto frothed egg whites and keep beating in high speed until stiff peaks form.
Let it cool down before folding in the almond paste.
Pour mixture into piping bag and pipe one-inch dollops on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Tap on the counter several times to release air bubbles.
Sprinkle with granulated sugar on top.

Completely cool macaron.

details.method:
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar and salt. With a pastry cutter or your fingers, gradually work the butter into the flour until
pea-sized pieces form. In a small bowl, stir together the egg yolk and water, then stir into the flour mixture using a fork.
Stir, then knead the dough together until it is no longer crumbly and holds together when pinched with your fingers. Form it into a disc
and wrap it tightly with plastic wrap. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour. On a lightly floured surface, roll the dough into a circle. Transfer the
crust to a round fluted tart pan with a removable bottom.
Press the crust into the pan and trim the edges. Place the crust in the refrigerator for 60 minutes (or freezer for 30 minutes). Preheat the
oven to 210˚C during the last 20 minutes of chilling the crust. Line the inside of the crust with parchment paper, then fill with baking
weights or dried beans.
Bake until the edges of the crust are very lightly golden, 10 to 12 minutes. Remove the pie weights and parchment paper, and prick the
bottom of the crust with a fork, 6 to 8 times. Return to the oven and bake until the whole crust is golden brown all over, 8 to 12 minutes
longer. Let cool to room temperature

details.method:
Preparation:
Jareesh: -
In a pot, sauté onion in ghee or oil. - Add jareesh and rice, stir briefly. - Add yogurt, water, spices, and salt. - Simmer on low heat for 1-1.5
hours until soft and creamy. - Mash lightly if desired to achieve a creamy texture.
Qursan: -
In another pot, sauté onion in oil. - Add tomato, bell pepper, and tomato paste, stir. - Add zucchini, potatoes, and pumpkin, stir for a few
minutes. - Add boiling water and spices, simmer until vegetables are cooked. - Break the qursan bread into pieces and add to the pot.-
Stir until the bread absorbs the sauce and softens. Let simmer until thickened.
Rice with lamb: - Boil lamb with onion and spices until fully cooked. - Remove and roast the lamb. - Cook basmati rice in the same broth

details.method:
Beef/lamb/chicken bones can be used
Mushroom trimmings
Fresh rosemary or thyme leaves trimmings
Fresh parsley leaves trimmings
Bay leaves
Black peppercorns all as per need
Method
Preheat the oven to 220°C. Place the bones in a large roasting pot with half of the oil and roast in the oven until golden brown,
turning occasionally. This should take 1 hour.
Meanwhile, place the vegetables with the garlic in a stockpot or large saucepan with the remaining oil.
Fry gently until lightly colored, turning occasionally.
Stir in the tomato puree and continue cooking until everything is golden brown then pour the red wine.
Reduce the liquid by boiling gently until it acquires a syrupy consistency.
Once the bones have a rich color, drain them of any fat using kitchen paper towels if necessary.
Add them to the vegetables along with the water.
Bring the water to the boil, skim off the scum that rises using a ladle, then add the herbs, bay leaves and black peppercorns.
Simmer very gently for about 10 hours, skimming off any further scum that accumulates on the surface.
Strain the stock by pouring the contents of the pan through a musli-lines colander set over a large bowl. Discard the bones,
vegetables and the herbs etc.
Wipe out the stockpot or saucepan and return the stock to the pan.
Boil down again until reduced by half or until it has reached sauce consistently.
Cool and use as required

Combine Beef with Spices: Add the seared beef back into the pan and mix well. Ensure the beef is evenly coated with the spices.

needed to prevent it from sticking to the pan. Stir occasionally, and let the beef cook until tender and the flavors are well absorbed.

Garnish and Serve: Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

details.method:
Combine the cornstarch and the beef cut into strips mix well for the beef strips to be fully and evenly coated in cornstarch.
Preheat a large skillet over high heat, then add enough oil to coat the bottom of the skillet. Next,add the bell peppers and quickly cook
them for about 3-4 minutes, stirring often. As soon as the bell peppers are browned slightly, remove them to a separate bowl. Do not
overcook them, they should still have a bit of a bite to them.
Add the onions to the skillet and sear for about 3-4 minutes, just trying to char up the sides. Add more oil if needed. Tilt the skillet and
remove the onion to the bowl with peppers, leaving the oil behind.
Next, add the rest of the oil and add the beef strips, shaking off the excess of cornstarch and cook in a single layer in batches for about 1
minute per side. Transfer the cooked beef to a separate bowl. Do not overcrowd the pan. Beef needs to be seared, not cooked in its own
juices. Keep adding the oil as needed after cooking each batch.
Mongolian Beef Sauce
Drain off the remaining oil from the skillet leaving the stuck on beef bits.
Next add the soy sauce, the oyster sauce, water and the sugar, the fresh ginger, minced garlic to the pan and let it come to a boil,
scraping off the bits off the bottom of the skillet. Boil for about 1-2 minutes to reduce the sauce. Then, add dried red chilies and the chili
flakes.
Bring everything together
Add the beef back into the sauce and stir to coat it in the sauce. Allow to come to a boil, which should thicken the sauce. Next add the
bell peppers, cooked onion, and the green onion stalks and stir to heat through.
Garnish with green onion

details.method:
Sauté the Onions:
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and mustard seeds and let them splutter. Then, add finely chopped onions and sauté them until they turn golden brown (this
step brings out a rich flavor).
Add Ginger-Garlic Paste:
Add the ginger-garlic paste to the pot and sauté for a minute until the raw smell disappears.
Add Tomatoes and Spices:
Add chopped tomatoes, along with coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and salt. Stir well.
Cook this mixture until the oil separates from the masala (spice mix) and the tomatoes soften. If needed, add a splash of water to prevent
burning.
Cook the Beef:
Add the beef to the pot and brown them for a few minutes, stirring occasionally to coat the beef in the spices.
Once the beef is browned, add water or beef broth and bring it to a boil. If using a pressure cooker, close the lid and cook for about 15-20
minutes (or until tender). If cooking in a regular pot, cover and cook on low heat for 1-1.5 hours, or until the beef is tender and the gravy
thickens. Stir occasionally, adding water as needed.
Add Yogurt:
If you want a creamy texture, add yogurt at this stage, and cook for another 5-10 minutes. Stir the yogurt in well, and let it simmer to blend
the flavors.
Garnish and Serve:
Once the beef is tender and the gravy is rich, sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander leaves on top.

details.method:
repare the Mutton: Wash the mutton pieces and drain excess water. You can optionally marinate the mutton in some yogurt, salt,
and spices (coriander powder, cumin powder, and turmeric) for 30 minutes to an hour for better flavor.
Fry Onions and Temper Spices: In a large pan, heat ghee or oil over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Then,
add the sliced onions and sauté until golden brown and caramelized (around 10 minutes).
Add Ginger-Garlic Paste and Chilies: Add ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Cook until the raw smell disappears (about 2
minutes).
Cook the Mutton: Add the mutton pieces to the pan and sear them until browned on all sides (about 5-7 minutes). This will give
the mutton a nice caramelization and flavor.
Add Spices: Sprinkle in the coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chili powder, and garam masala powder. Stir
well and let the spices cook for a minute or two to release their aroma.
Incorporate Cashew or Almond Paste: Add the cashew paste or almond paste. Stir it in well to form a creamy base. If you're using
poppy seeds, you can grind them with a little water to make a paste and add it now.
Add Yogurt: Lower the heat and add the whisked yogurt, stirring continuously to avoid curdling. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until
the yogurt blends with the spices and forms a thick gravy.
Add Water: Pour in water to adjust the gravy to your desired consistency. You can make it more or less thick, depending on your
preference. Cover and cook the mutton for 40-45 minutes on low heat until the mutton becomes tender. If using a pressure
cooker, cook for about 15-20 minutes after the first whistle.
Add Cream and Lemon Juice: Once the mutton is cooked, add cream for a rich finish. Stir it in well, and then check for seasoning.
Add salt and a squeeze of lemon juice for a slight tanginess.
Garnish and Serve: Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.

details.method:
Prepare the Cauliflower:
Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
In a large bowl, combine the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, pepper, and garlic powder (optional).
Add water to the dry ingredients and stir until a thick batter forms. Add more water if needed to achieve a pancake-like batter
consistency.
Toss the cauliflower florets into the batter, ensuring they are evenly coated.
2.Fry the Cauliflower:
Heat a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat and add about 2 tablespoons of cooking oil.
Once the oil is hot, add the cauliflower florets in batches, making sure not to overcrowd the pan.
Fry the cauliflower for 3-4 minutes per side, or until golden brown and crispy. Remove from the pan and drain on paper towels to
remove excess oil.
3.Make the General Tso's Sauce:
In a small bowl, combine the soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and water.
In a separate small bowl, dissolve the cornstarch in 1 tablespoon of water and set aside.
Heat a pan over medium heat and add a little oil. Once hot, sauté the minced ginger and garlic for about 1-2 minutes, or until
fragrant.
Pour in the sauce mixture and bring it to a simmer. Once it starts to thicken, add the cornstarch slurry (the cornstarch and water
mixture) to the sauce and stir. Continue cooking for another 2-3 minutes, until the sauce is thick and glossy.
If you want some spice, add chili paste or chili flakes to the sauce and stir well.
4.Combine Cauliflower with Sauce:
Add the crispy cauliflower florets to the pan with the General Tso's sauce. Toss gently to coat all the florets with the sauce. Cook for
2-3 minutes to heat everything through.
5.Serve:
Transfer the General Tso's Cauliflower to a serving dish.
Garnish with sesame seeds and chopped green onions.
Serve immediately with steamed rice or as an appetizer!

details.method:
grind garlic and ginger into paste
inse the bhindi (okra) well in water for a couple of times.
Dry them on a large plate on their own or wipe with a kitchen towel. Make sure there is no moisture or water on the okra pods.
Remove the base and stalk while chopping them. Chop into 1 or 1.5 inch pieces.
Also chop onions and tomatoes. Keep aside.
Make a paste of ginger and garlic in mortar-pestle and keep aside.
Sautéing bhindi
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a kadai (wok) or pan.
Add the chopped bhindi and sauté stirring often till they are completely cooked. You will have to keep an eye on them and stir in between
many times.
Taste the sautéed okra and if the crunchiness is not there and the bhindi have become soft, it means they are cooked. Keep the sautéed
bhindi aside.
Sautéing onions, tomatoes, spices
All the oil will be used up. So add 1 tablespoon oil to the same pan.
Add chopped onions and sauté stirring often on low to medium heat till they become translucent and are softened.
Add the ginger-garlic paste and sauté on low heat for a few seconds or till the raw aroma of the ginger-garlic disappears.
Add the chopped tomatoes and saute stirring often till the tomatoes become soft and mushy.
If the tomato mixture becomes too dry and starts sticking to the pan, then add about ¼ cup water. Mix well and continue to cook.
All the above cooking is done in a open pan and you don't need to cover the pan with the lid.
Add all the dry ground spice powders one by one.
Mix well and saute for a few seconds on low heat.
Making bhindi masala
Add the sautéed bhindi, crushed kasuri methi, salt and mix so that the onion-tomato masala coats the okra well.
Cook for about 2 minutes. Stir in between.
Then turn off the heat and add chopped coriander leaves. Mix again.

details.ingredients:
Grilled Beef Tenderloin - 2kg
Puff Pastry Sheets - Sunbulah - 300g
Extra Virgin Olive Oil - 60ml
Grilled Turkey Bacon - 150g
Eggs - Saeed Co. Farmer - 60g
Sea Salt - Natureland - 1g
Dijon Mustard - Freshly - 60g
Mushroom, Sanitized - 1kg
details.method:
1. Allow the oven to preheat to 400°F as you assemble the Wellington.
2. Brush the beef with mustard:
brush the beef on all sides with mustard.
3. Wrap the beef in mushroom paste and Bacon:
Roll out a large piece of plastic wrap. Lay out the slices of bacon on the plastic wrap so that they overlap and are large enough to wrap
around and encapsulate the beef. Spread the mushroom mixture over the bacon.
Place the beef in the middle and roll the mushroom and bacon over the beef, using the plastic wrap so that you do this tightly.
Wrap up the beef into a tight barrel shape, twisting the ends of the plastic wrap to secure. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
4. Roll out the puff pastry and wrap the beef:
On a lightly floured surface, roll out the puff pastry sheet to a size that will wrap around the beef.
Unwrap the beef from the plastic wrap and place in the middle of the pastry dough. Brush the edges of the pastry with the beaten egg
yolks.
Fold the pastry around the beef, cutting off any excess at the ends. (Pastry that is more than 2 layers thick will not cook all the way, try to
limit the overlap.)
Place on a small plate, seam side down, and brush beaten egg yolks all over the top. Chill for 5 to 10 minutes.
5. Brush with the egg wash and score:
Place the pastry-wrapped beef on a baking pan. Brush the exposed surface again with beaten eggs.
Score the top of the pastry with a sharp knife, not going all the way through the pastry. Sprinkle the top with coarse salt.
6. Bake in the oven:
Bake at 400°F for 25 to 35 minutes. The pastry should be nicely golden when done. To ensure that your roast is medium rare, test with a
thermometer. Pull out at 125 to 130°F for medium rare.

Rice in pan - Place the rice in a 20cm / 8" square pan (metal or ceramic). Add pandam or kaffir, if using.

Transfer the Aubergine Caviar to a serving bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to meld together.

Garnish with additional chopped parsley or a drizzle of olive oil, if desired.
Serve with toasted bread, crackers, or as a spread for sandwiches.

details.method:
Making the Dosa:
Prepare the Pan:
Heat a non-stick or cast-iron tawa (griddle) over medium-high heat. Once hot, reduce the heat slightly. Sprinkle a few drops of water on the tawa;
if it sizzles and evaporates immediately, the tawa is ready.
Spreading the Batter:
Pour a ladleful of batter in the center of the tawa. Quickly spread it outward in a circular motion using the back of the ladle to form a thin layer.
Cooking the Dosa:
Drizzle a few drops of oil or ghee around the edges and on top of the dosa. Cook until the edges start to lift and the underside turns golden brown
and crisp.
If you prefer, you can flip the dosa and cook the other side for a few seconds, but traditionally, dosa is cooked on one side only.

Add the boneless chicken breast, shrimp, calamari, chopped parsley, and rice to the pot. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour the chicken broth slowly around the pan and jiggle the pan to get the rice into an even layer.
Bring mixture to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low. Give the pan a gentle shake back and forth once or twice during cooking. (By not
stirring the rice, we create a delectable crispy crust at the bottom, known as socarrat.)
Cook for about 15-18 minutes (uncovered), sprinkle peas on top, and
continue to cook (without stirring) for about five more minutes.
Watch for most of the liquid to be absorbed and for the rice at the top to be nearly tender. (If for some reason your rice is still not
cooked, add ¼
cup more broth and continue cooking).
Remove the pan from heat and cover it with a lid or tinfoil. Place a kitchen towel over the lid and allow it to rest for 10 minutes.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley and lemon slices.

details.method:
For the Jackfruit Asado:
2 cans of young green jackfruit in water or brine, drained and rinsed (approximately 500 grams)
15 grams olive oil
1 onion, finely chopped (about 150 grams)
3 cloves garlic, minced (about 15 grams)
5 grams ground cumin
5 grams smoked paprika
5 grams chili powder
2.5 grams ground coriander
2.5 grams oregano
1 gram cayenne pepper (optional, for extra heat)
240 grams vegetable broth
30 grams soy sauce or tamari
30 grams tomato paste
Salt and pepper to taste
For the Tacos:
Taco Shells
Fresh cilantro, chopped
Lime wedges
Sliced avocado
Pickled red onions
Salsa or hot sauce
Instructions:
1. Prepare the Jackfruit:
Shred the jackfruit using your hands or a fork to create a pulled texture.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and garlic, and sauté until softened and fragrant, about 5
minutes.
Add the shredded jackfruit to the skillet, along with the cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, ground coriander, oregano, and
cayenne pepper. Stir well to coat the jackfruit with the spices.
Pour in the vegetable broth, soy sauce, and tomato paste. Stir to combine. Reduce the heat to low and let the mixture simmer
for about 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the jackfruit is tender and the flavors are well combined. Season with salt
and pepper to taste.
2. Assemble the Tacos:
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or microwave.
Fill each tortilla with a generous amount of the jackfruit asado.
Top with fresh cilantro, sliced avocado, pickled red onions, and a squeeze of lime juice.
Add salsa

stuffing from earlier, stuff them in each squid. If you happen to run out of this, feel free to make more using the same ratio for
ingredients. Now we’re all prepped and ready to go with grilling!

For grilling, you have to keep a close eye on your squid. Remember that it can be very easy to end up with a rubbery squid, and so be
careful not to overcook it. To get it tender while cooked all the way through, grill the first side of your pusit for 6 to 8 minutes. Then turn
each squid over, and grill it for the same amount of time.

vinegar (optional)

'In a large pot, heat the vegetable oil over medium-high heat.
Season the beef with salt and pepper, add it to the pot in batches, and brown it on all sides. Remove the browned meat and set it aside.
Add the chopped onions to the same pot and cook until they are soft and translucent about 5 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle the all-purpose flour over the onions and garlic, stirring to coat evenly. Cook for 2-3 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste.
Return the browned beef to the pot, along with any accumulated juices.
Add the tomato paste, paprika, and caraway seeds to the pot, stirring to combine and coat the meat and vegetables.
Pour in the apple cider vinegar and beef broth, stirring to deglaze the bottom of the pot and loosen any browned bits.
Add the diced carrots, diced potatoes, chopped bell peppers, and canned diced tomatoes to the pot. Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer, reduce the heat to low, and cover the pot with a lid.
Let the beef goulash simmer gently for about 2-3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the meat is tender and the flavors have melded together.
Taste the goulash and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve the beef goulash hot, garnished with fresh parsley.

to 160*C no steam. Put the savarin in the oven at 160øC and leave them to cook for 8 minutes (turn the trays halfway through cooking).
Take them out of the oven, remove them from the moulds and put them back in the oven on a baking tray for 5 minutes at 160 øC to
brown them. Take the out and leave them to cool.
For the syrup and soaking the savarin:
Put the savarin to soak in the syrup for 20 minutes, then strain for 20 minutes, before re-soaking them in the syrup. Put them in the
chiller for 10 minutes, then apply the neutral glaze to the savarin with a brush and put them to one side on a rack.
For the chantilly passion:
Brunoise (finely dice) the mangos and the pineapple. Caramelized half of the diced mangoes and pine apple in the olive oil and lemon
juice. Deglaze with the passion fruit pulp, add the diced papaya. Leave to cool. Fill the center of each savarin with the mixture. Using a
bag fitted with a star piping nozzle, create a rose shape to cover the center of the savarin. Sprinkle with the remaining diced mangos,
pineapple and papaya and add a light sprinkling of lime zest to decorate.

details.method:
'Prepare the Tortilla:
Peel the potatoes and cut them into small cubes.
Finely chop the onion and bell peppers if using.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the potatoes to the skillet and cook until they are tender and lightly browned, stirring occasionally.
Add the chopped onion and bell peppers to the skillet and cook until softened.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper.

Pour the egg and vegetable mixture into the skillet and spread it out evenly.

Carefully flip the tortilla using a large plate or lid to cover the skillet, and cook the other side until it is cooked through and golden brown.
Assemble the Bocadillos:
Cut the baguettes or bread rolls in half lengthwise.
Cut the cooked tortilla into squares or wedges, depending on the size of your bread.
Place a portion of the tortilla on the bottom half of each baguette or bread roll.

Drain the canned tuna and flake it with a fork.

Drain the capers.
Assemble the Pan Bagnat:
Slice the top off each bread loaf and set them aside. Hollow out the inside of each loaf, leaving a shell.
Drizzle olive oil and red wine vinegar over the inside of each bread loaf.
Layer the bottom of each bread loaf with the flaked tuna, followed by the sliced tomatoes, red onion, bell peppers, cucumber, black olives, anchovy
fillets (if using), and capers.

Press and Chill:
Wrap each Pan Bagnat tightly in plastic wrap.
Place a heavy object, such as a cast-iron skillet or cans of food, on top of the sandwiches to press them down.
Refrigerate the pressed sandwiches for at least 2 hours, or overnight if possible. This allows the flavors to meld together and the bread to absorb
the juices from the filling.
Slice and Serve:
Unwrap the chilled Pan Bagnat sandwiches and carefully slice them into wedges.
Garnish each wedge with fresh basil leaves if desired.
Serve the sandwiches immediately, and enjoy the flavors of this classic French picnic dish!

Place the beef in a large resealable plastic bag or a shallow dish, and pour the marinade over the beef. Make sure the beef is well coated.
Marinate the beef in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or overnight for best flavor.
Cook the Beef:
Preheat the oven to 160øC (325øF).
Transfer the marinated beef to a roasting pan and cover it with aluminum foil.
Roast the beef in the preheated oven for 3-4 hours, or until it is tender and easily shreds with a fork.
Once cooked, remove the beef from the oven and let it cool slightly before shredding it with two forks.
Assemble the Sandwiches:
Spread mayonnaise and mustard on one side of each sandwich roll or bread slice.
Place a generous amount of shredded beef on the bottom half of each roll or bread slice.
Top the beef with sliced onion, bell pepper , tomato, and lettuce leaves.
Cover with the top half of the roll or another slice of bread.

details.method:
'Preheat your oven to 180øC (350øF).
Grease a large baking dish with butter.
Arrange a layer of sliced sweet potatoes in the bottom of the baking dish, overlapping them slightly.
Sprinkle a portion of minced garlic, fresh thyme leaves, salt, and pepper over the sweet potatoes.
Repeat the layers until all the sweet potatoes, garlic, and thyme are used, ending with a layer of sweet potatoes on top.
In a mixing bowl, combine the heavy cream and grated Gruyere cheese. Mix well.
Pour the cream and cheese mixture over the layered sweet potatoes in the baking dish, ensuring that it covers the potatoes evenly.
Sprinkle the grated Parmesan cheese over the top of the gratin.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil and bake in the preheated oven for about 45-50 minutes.
After 45-50 minutes, remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 15-20 minutes, or until the sweet potatoes are tender and the top is
golden brown and bubbly.
Once cooked, remove the gratin from the oven and let it rest for a few minutes before serving.

'Rinse the brown rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain well.
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and bell peppers, and cook until softened, about 5
minutes.
Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, chili powder, ground cumin, and dried oregano. Cook for 1-2 minutes to toast the spices.
Add the brown rice to the pot and stir to coat it evenly with the vegetable mixture.
Pour in enough water to cover the rice by about 2.5 cm (1 inch). Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 40-

'In a large pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and saut‚ for 5-7 minutes until softened.

Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and let it simmer for about 30-40 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are

Once the stew is cooked and the vegetables are tender, remove it from the heat.
Serve the Hungarian Lentil Vegetable Stew hot, garnished with fresh parsley if desired.
Optionally, you can serve the stew with a dollop of vegan sour cream on top for added creaminess.

name: Slow Roast Duck With Apple Stuffing

details.ingredients:

details.method:
Cooking the Coq au Vin:
Remove the chicken pieces from the marinade and pat them dry with paper towels. Reserve the marinade and vegetables separately.
In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, cook the diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon and set
it aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pot.
Dredge the chicken pieces in all-purpose flour, shaking off any excess.
In the same pot with the bacon fat, brown the chicken pieces in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove the chicken and set it aside.
Add the unsalted butter to the pot and melt it over medium heat.
Add the pearl onions, diced carrots, and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Saut‚ until the vegetables are softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic, fresh thyme leaves, and tomato paste. Cook for another 2 minutes.
Return the cooked bacon and browned chicken pieces to the pot.
Pour in the reserved marinade (strained from the vegetables and herbs) and chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let the Coq au Vin simmer gently for about 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the chicken is tender and cooked
through, and the sauce has thickened.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper if needed.
Before serving, sprinkle chopped fresh parsley over the Coq au Vin as a garnish.

details.ingredients:
Cabbage, White, Sliced - 2kg
Fennel, Sanitized - 1kg

Vegetables Broth - 1kg

Ground Black Pepper - FRESHLY - 5g

details.method:
'In a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot, heat the olive oil over medium heat.
Add the minced garlic and sliced onions to the pot and saute‚ for about 3-4 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Add the sliced cabbage and fennel to the pot. Stir to combine with the onions and garlic.
Pour the vegetable broth over the vegetables in the pot. The broth should partially cover the vegetables; if necessary, add a little water to ensure
they're mostly submerged.
Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low. Cover the pot and let the vegetables braise for about 30-40 minutes, or until they are
tender and flavorful.
Stir occasionally during cooking and check the liquid level; if it evaporates too quickly, add more vegetable broth or water as needed.
Once the vegetables are tender, season the braised cabbage and fennel with salt and pepper to taste.
Remove the pot from the heat and transfer the braised vegetables to a serving dish.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley if desired.

details.ingredients:

details.method:
'Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the sliced mushrooms to the pot and cook until they release their liquid and start to brown,
about 10 minutes. Remove the mushrooms from the pot and set aside.
In the same pot, add the pearl onions, carrots, and celery. Cook for about 5 minutes until they begin to soften.
Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables in the pot and stir well to coat them evenly.
Slowly pour in the red wine, stirring constantly to deglaze the pot and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom.
Stir in the tomato paste, vegetable broth, smoked paprika, fresh thyme leaves, salt, and pepper.
Return the cooked mushrooms to the pot and stir everything together until well combined.
Cover the pot and let the Mushroom Bourguignon simmer over low heat for about 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are
tender and the sauce has thickened.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper if needed. Stir in the chopped parsley just before serving.

details.ingredients:
Lamb, Shoulder, Defrosted - 1.8kg
Iodized Table Salt - Sasa - 10g
Ground Black Pepper - FRESHLY - 5g
Olive Pomace Oil - Freshly - 60ml
Onion, White, Diced - 300g

details.method:
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the lamb cubes in batches, ensuring they don't overcrowd the pan. Sear the
lamb for about 4 minutes per se until browned. Once seared, remove the lamb from the pot and set ase. In the same pot, reduce the heat
to medium and add the chopped onion. Sauté for about 3 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, carrots, and celery. Cook for an
additional 5 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften. Pour in the balsamic vinegar, scraping the bottom of the pot with a spoon to
release any browned bits from the lamb and vegetables. Allow the vinegar to cook for about 2 minutes, letting some of the acity reduce.
Stir in the tomato paste, broth, brown sugar, thyme, rosemary, and bay leaf. Mix well to combine. Return the lamb to the pot, along with
any juices that have accumulated on the plate. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce the heat to
low. Cover the pot and let it simmer for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until the lamb is tender and the flavors have melded together. Stir occasionally
to prevent sticking, and check the seasoning. Once the lamb is tender, remove the bay leaf and adjust seasoning if necessary (add more
salt, pepper, or sugar if you like a sweeter sauce). Serve the stew in bowls, garnished with freshly chopped parsley.

details.ingredients:

Combine warm water, milk, active yeast, sugar, and oil. Whisk to let yeast and sugar dissolve, then let it sit

Meanwhile combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a stand mixer. You can mix with your hands too if
you prefer.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredient mixture. Start on low speed to slowly incorporate all the
ingredients together then on medium speed until it becomes a dough shape. Keep kneading for 3 to 4
minutes on medium speed.
The dough should be elastic and really soft but not stick to your fingers or on the mixing bowl.
Take the dough off the hook and form it into a ball. Place back to the mixing bowl, cover with plastic wrap
and let it rise in a warm place until it becomes triple in size, about 2 hours. Let it sit longer if needed.

if you do, use as minimal as possible. Cut the dough circle with a ring mold.

In a large pan, melt 100 grams of butter over medium heat.

Gradually add the milk, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
